title: zone-map plugin declares group and type, identical on 12 of 12 seed entities
body:
## Summary
The zone-map gap plugin histograms `group` and `type`, which hold the same value on every seeded zone, so one dimension is reported twice.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/plugins/zone-map.ts:4 declares `['group', 'type']`. On the code seed both histograms are {hub:2, combat:8, boss:2} and per entity `data.group === data.type` holds 12/12. The landing view (src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/landing.ts:95) reads them as two independent dimensions. Fixed = one of them replaced by a dimension that varies independently (seed candidates: `status`, a levelRange band), or the duplicate dropped. Which carries design meaning is a pick on the zone vocabulary.

## Flow
- probe: codeSeededEntities('zone-map').filter(e => e.data.group === e.data.type).length -> 12 of 12
- add a ratchet: no plugin declares two dimensions equal on >=90% of its seed entities (seeded red on zone-map)
- replace `group` with the chosen independent dimension; ratchet green

## Expected impact
The one-shot landing panel stops showing the same zone bucket twice; a future zone-map expectedShare cannot double-weight one axis. Risk: a consumer keyed on byAttribute.group.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one zone dimension measured once, not twice
Before: 2 of 2 declared zone-map dimensions identical on 12/12 seed entities
After: predicted 0 duplicated dimensions (not built: replacement dimension is a vocabulary pick)
Method: probe - per-entity equality on the code seed; the fix needs a choice of replacement dimension
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: coverage-ratchet case: per plugin, no two declared dimensions agree on >=90% of seed entities

title: loot-tables plugin measures nothing: its one dimension is degenerate on the seed
body:
## Summary
The loot-tables plugin declares only `archetypeName`, unique on all 22 seed entities, so the catalog gets an empty histogram.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/plugins/loot-tables.ts:4 declares `['archetypeName']`; measureDimensions (src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/coverage.ts:86) marks it degenerate (22 singleton buckets > SAMPLE_MAX), so byAttribute = {}. The seed carries no categorical field (archetypeId/lootTableName also unique; dropChance, bonusGold numeric; rarityWeights an object). Fixed = a dimension that distributes the catalog, e.g. the dominant rarity of `rarityWeights` or a dropChance band, which needs a derived-dimension hook in GapAnalysisPlugin (plugins/types.ts) or a seed field. Pinned in DEGENERATE_PLUGIN_ALLOWLIST (src/__tests__/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/coverage-ratchet.test.ts).

## Flow
- analyzeCatalog('loot-tables', codeSeededEntities('loot-tables')) -> byAttribute {}, degenerate [archetypeName]
- add an optional derived-dimension reader to GapAnalysisPlugin (or a seed field)
- declare it; remove loot-tables from DEGENERATE_PLUGIN_ALLOWLIST

## Expected impact
Loot tables get a real distribution in the one-shot Analyze view and can later carry an expected share. Risk: extending the plugin type touches every reader of `dimensions` (landing, closurePlan, ratchet).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - loot-tables histogram non-empty
Before: byAttribute {} on 22 seed entities (1 of 1 dimension degenerate)
After: predicted >=1 measured dimension; not built (plugin type change, M)
Method: probe - analyzeCatalog on the code seed; After needs the derived-dimension mechanism
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: DEGENERATE_PLUGIN_ALLOWLIST in coverage-ratchet.test.ts shrinks from [loot-tables] to []

title: A degenerate-only catalog gets no histogram and no facet fallback
body:
## Summary
When every declared dimension is degenerate, analyzeCatalog returns an empty byAttribute and skips the envelope-facet fallback that stale plugins receive.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/index.ts:115 (post-fix numbering) runs the facet fallback only when `degenerate.length === 0`. A stale plugin (all dimensions unmeasured) gets @category/@lifecycle; a degenerate-only plugin (loot-tables on its seed) gets nothing, so the Analyze view shows no distribution. facets.ts:1-8 says facets exist so a catalog still has a histogram. Whether a degenerate report should suppress the facets is a reading of intent; the comment above the guard names only the stale case.

## Flow
- analyzeCatalog('loot-tables', seed) -> byAttribute {}
- change the guard to "no measured histogram" (byAttribute empty) regardless of degenerate
- test: loot-tables seed has @lifecycle; healthy catalogs unchanged

## Expected impact
Every catalog with entities shows at least an envelope histogram. Risk: a UI that reads any @ key as "plugin stale" would mislabel a degenerate catalog.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every non-empty catalog shows a histogram
Before: 1 of 37 sectioned catalogs (loot-tables) returns byAttribute {} with 22 entities
After: predicted 0 of 37
Method: probe - analyzeCatalog over every code seed; not built because the guard may be deliberate (degenerate reported instead)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: facets.test.ts case: a degenerate-only catalog gets @lifecycle; red on base tree

title: Only 2 of 32 gap plugins declare an expected share, so 30 catalogs never rank
body:
## Summary
Gap ranking needs a declared expectedShare; only items and bestiary have one, so every other catalog is listed unmeasured indefinitely.

## Description
rankCatalogGaps (src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/rankGaps.ts:60-73) ranks only catalogs whose gapBasis is expected-share. Only plugins/items.ts:5 and plugins/bestiary.ts:5 declare one. Catalogs with fully measured categorical dimensions and no share: spellbook (tier/element/category, 70 entities), state-graph (category, 86), zone-map (type, 12), characters (role). Their target mix is a GDD decision (what fraction of spells should be Ultimate?), not something code can infer, so the shares must come from the operator or the GDD.

## Flow
- operator states target shares for spellbook tier/element/category and state-graph category
- declare them in the plugins; the plugin contract test (plugins.test.ts) checks they key declared dimensions and sum to ~1
- GET /api/one-shot/gaps then ranks those catalogs

## Expected impact
The gap-first one-shot flow covers 6 catalogs instead of 2. Risk: invented shares would manufacture gaps, which is why this is the operator's call.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - more catalogs get ranked gaps
Before: 2 of 32 plugins with expectedShare; 30 catalogs always unmeasured
After: unmeasurable until target shares exist
Method: probe - counted expectedShare declarations; the After figure needs design targets no instrument supplies
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
grep expectedShare src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/plugins/*.ts -> items.ts, bestiary.ts only
probe spellbook by={tier:{basic:33,advanced:29,ultimate:8},...} basis none

title: affixes catalog has no gap plugin and falls back to inference
body:
## Summary
The affixes section has no gap-analysis plugin; it is histogrammed by inferred keys (affixTag, isPrefix, group) instead of declared ones.

## Description
affixes is in CATALOG_SECTIONS but has no file under src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/plugins/, so analyzeCatalog uses inferDimensions (src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/index.ts). Its seed carries categorical fields group, isPrefix, minRarity, statTarget. A plugin declaring them (summarize displayName/group) gives an intended distribution; affixTag is an identity key that inference still picks. Pinned in NO_PLUGIN_ALLOWLIST (coverage-ratchet.test.ts). The other four no-plugin catalogs (story-arcs, contracts, player-movement, character-pipeline) are pipeline exemplars whose seeds carry only a description; gap analysis may be not-applicable there.

## Flow
- add plugins/affixes.ts: dimensions [group, isPrefix, minRarity], summarize displayName/group
- import it in plugins/index.ts
- remove affixes from NO_PLUGIN_ALLOWLIST; the derived plugin contract test covers it automatically

## Expected impact
Affix proposals get a distribution of the fields that matter instead of a unique-tag histogram. Risk: none beyond the new file.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - affixes measured on declared dimensions
Before: 1 of 3 inferred affixes dimensions is an identity key (affixTag)
After: predicted 0 of 3
Method: probe - analyzeCatalog on the 1-entity code seed; n=1 cannot show a distribution, so the gain is predicted
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: NO_PLUGIN_ALLOWLIST in coverage-ratchet.test.ts shrinks by affixes

title: Two deficit definitions: rankGaps uses rounded expected, closurePlan the raw share
body:
## Summary
rankCatalogGaps orders targets by `round(share*total) - count` while planClosure orders gaps by `share*total - got`, so the two can disagree on which gap is largest.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/rankGaps.ts:66 sets `deficit: u.expected - u.count` with the Math.round-ed expected from index.ts; src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/closurePlan.ts:44 uses the unrounded `s * d.total - got`. Two gaps with raw deficits 2.4 and 1.6 both rank as 2 in rankGaps and fall to alphabetical order, while the closure plan fills the 2.4 one first. Distinct from the recorded scoring-rubrics deviation (no impact/effort estimate). Fixed = one deficit rule exported once and used by both.

## Flow
- construct a distribution with two under-represented buckets whose raw deficits round to the same integer
- compare rankCatalogGaps order with the planClosure first assignment
- export a single gapDeficit(got, share, total) and use it in both

## Expected impact
The "what next" list and the closure plan agree on the top gap. Risk: a fractional GapTarget.deficit changes the on-screen number unless display rounds.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - ranking and closure plan agree on order
Before: two deficit formulas at 2 sites
After: predicted 1 formula; disagreement shown only in walked cases
Method: simulation - walked the 2.4 vs 1.6 case by hand; no seed catalog hits it today (items and bestiary gaps differ by >=5)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/rankGaps.ts:66 deficit: u.expected - u.count
src/lib/catalog/gap-analysis/closurePlan.ts:44 deficit: s * d.total - got
instrument: rankGaps.test.ts case with two near-tied gaps asserting rank order equals planClosure order
